title: Where a switch can go
body: A switch is a gap you can open and close. When it's closed, it's just part of the wire. When it's open, it breaks the loop.
In one loop, the electricity moves like a bike chain: it all moves together. Break the loop anywhere and the whole flow stops at once. That's true before the bulb and after it.
So a switch works on either side of the bulb. Near the battery's plus end or its minus end, it does the same job.
realWorld: Every light switch at home works like this. Flick it off and it opens a gap. Then the flow stops all the way round the loop.
sources: OpenStax College Physics 2e, §21.1 Resistors in Series and Parallel. https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/21-1-resistors-in-series-and-parallel
